subject: Private deployment intake — runbook checks and evidence schedule
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@onyxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment intake — runbook checks and evidence schedule

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the kick-off call yesterday. To keep momentum, attaching our intake checklist (redwood_prereq_checklist_v1.xlsx) and a lightweight network diagram stub that outlines the places we usually need evidence. Can you please: 

- Confirm the account contact who will provide VPC/subnet CIDRs, peering details, and a list of service accounts with KMS access.
- Upload the inventory template (we attached the stub) with IP ranges and a copy of your current firewall allowlist.
- Share any constraints around egress (approved egress IPs, proxy requirements) and whether the environment will be air-gapped for the initial validation window.

We're proposing a short evidence run this Friday (May 24) 09:00–11:00 PT to validate connectivity and run a smoke traffic test. If that doesn't work, suggest two alternatives. Ben will lead the network validation; Grace will take the KMS/credentials handoff.

Key items we need before Friday morning:
- Completed inventory CSV (onyx_vpc_inventory.csv)
- Service account IAM roles exported (minimum: compute/networking/KMS)
- Firewall rules snapshot or firewall admin access for read-only evidence

Attachments:
- redwood_prereq_checklist_v1.xlsx (prereqs checklist)
- network-diagram-stub.pdf (illustrative)

Thanks — getting these early saves time on the dry run.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@onyxhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — runbook checks and evidence schedule

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the checklist and summary. Quick answers inline: 

- Account contact for artifacts: I (Daniel Park) will own the inventory. Procurement will copy in any legal/contract-level items.
- Egress: We have a constrained egress window for PHI environments — traffic must go through our managed NAT/Proxy (egress IPs are fixed). We will provide the approved egress IPs in the inventory.
- Air-gap: Not fully air-gapped, but network policy restricts external connections to whitelisted destinations only.

I've attached our preliminary inventory CSV (onyx_vpc_inventory.csv) — still cleaning it but includes CIDRs, VPC ids, and the two subnets we plan to use for the Redwood workers and bastion.

Friday 09:00–11:00 PT works for us, but we prefer a short kickoff at 09:00 and then the validation tests starting 09:30.

Two clarifications: 
1) For KMS access, we need details on what minimum roles Redwood needs so our security team can create a scoped service account.
2) Will Redwood require inbound ports opened to the workers, or can you validate purely from a bastion/proxy egress test?

Attaching: onyx_vpc_inventory.csv

—Daniel Park
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
OnyxHealth
Daniel.Park@onyxhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@onyxhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — runbook checks and evidence schedule

Thanks Daniel — this is great. A couple of operational notes from our side before Friday: 

- KMS roles: Redwood needs a service account with get/decrypt/encrypt on the KMS key used to wrap model keys, and IAM permission to read service account metadata. We'll send a minimal IAM policy snippet by EOD.
- Inbound ports: We do NOT require any open inbound ports from public internet to worker VMs. For the connectivity validation we will use the bastion you provide and perform egress-based smoke tests, plus a short TLS handshake from the bastion to the worker control plane over the peering link. If you prefer, the handshake can be initiated by your bastion to our test endpoint.
- Certificate pinning: for the control plane we will provide fingerprint to pin during the handshake; plan to exchange before testing.

I've proposed a 30-minute calendar invite (Friday 09:00–09:30 kickoff) and a 60-minute validation window (09:30–10:30). Grace — can you confirm who will hold the KMS keys and coordinate the service account creation with Onyx?

Forwarding the invite after we agree final times.

—Ben
Network & Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@onyxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@onyxhealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — runbook checks and evidence schedule

Perfect — thanks everyone. Summary / action items before Friday: 

1) Onyx (Daniel) — finalize and upload the inventory CSV with the final egress IPs and firewall snapshot (filesystem or SharePoint link). We need service account email and intended KMS key alias by Thursday EOD.
2) Redwood (Ben/Grace) — send the minimal IAM policy snippet for the KMS service account and the control-plane certificate fingerprint (we'll publish to the shared drive link).
3) Procurement (Onyx) — if there are any compliance gates (legal wording, data residency clauses), please flag them now; otherwise we'll proceed with the runbook validation scoped to network & credentials.

Calendar plan now: 
- 2028-05-24 09:00–09:30 PT: Kickoff (quick alignment)
- 2028-05-24 09:30–10:30 PT: Connectivity & smoke validation
- Buffer 10:30–11:00 PT for triage and next steps

Drive folder (temporary): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-redwood-intake-runbook — please drop the inventory and firewall snapshot there.

I'll send a short pre-call checklist to the drive and calendar attendees with the test commands we'll run so your ops team can be ready. Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

—Stephanie
Solutions Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
